items.note: Cross-cultural controlled experiment: 118 participants from India and the US write culturally grounded texts with and without GPT-4o suggestions; outcomes are efficiency and homogenization of writing style toward Western norms. Abstract does not say how conditions were assigned (likely within-person); same study as arXiv 2409.11360.

Systematic review and taxonomy of how human-AI co-creativity studies measure creativity; it reviews measurement methods rather than pooling effects, so it may be borderline for the synthesis category.
Topic-modelling systematic mapping review of 61 publications (2023 to June 2025) on generative AI and creativity; no pooled estimates, borderline between synthesis and narrative review.
Compares 46 human participants with ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemini 2.0 on AUT originality and RAT accuracy; no participant receives AI help.

Framework for ex ante crowding risk: diversity of generations from three frontier LLMs is compared with matched unaided human baselines on short stories, slogans, and AUT; no human-AI interaction data, so it is close to model-only (out_reason model_only is the alternative). Abstract from OpenAlex; the arXiv API timed out.

Randomised crossover: design-engineering undergraduates alternate between ChatGPT-assisted and unaided ideation; 728 ideas scored for fluency, flexibility, originality, thematic homogenisation, and semantic divergence, plus carryover by order. Number of students not in the abstract (check against 50).

52 participant pairs (104 people, unit of treatment is the pair) do the AUT with ChatGPT-4 access versus a no-AI control; outcomes are idea count, performance, and elaboration, including an unaided post-test (after_ai). Assignment method not stated.

Mixed-methods: qualitative study plus a quantitative study linking autonomy frustration and editing of AI output to objective creative performance; the abstract does not show a no-AI or alternative-AI condition, so the next stage should check whether Study 2 manipulates AI assistance (otherwise out). SSRN version listed as OpenAlex W4410156412.

78 fifth-graders randomly assigned to visual-art instruction using AI-generated images versus conventional images; paintings compared on creativity and originality among other criteria, plus self-reported engagement, self-efficacy, and cognitive load. AI is a teaching material rather than a tool students use while producing, so eligibility needs a check.

Representative US adults versus AI chatbots on creative ideas, plus humans augmented with AI (HumanPlusAI) and humans competing against AI, with blind creativity ratings; also contains AI-versus-human context evidence. Abstract (Crossref, SSRN) states no N or assignment method; search notes say the paper body reports random assignment.
